title: The $3,000 Debt That Takes 15 Years to Disappear
hook_text: THE STATEMENT YOU DON'T OPEN STILL COUNTS

beats.say: The statement you don’t open still counts. A $3,000 credit card at 24%minimum payments takes 15 years.
beats.visual: extreme close of a crumpled unopened envelope on a rain-slick iron table, sodium streetlight glare

beats.say: Why does ignoring it make it worse?
beats.visual: high angle shot of a phone face-down on a foggy bridge rail, cold blue light

beats.say: Most think: if I don’t look, the problem stays small. But interest never sleeps.
beats.visual: silhouette of a hand holding a closed banking app, towering city lights behind

beats.say: That $3,000 grows to $7,887 in payments. 15 years of your life.
beats.visual: extreme wide of an empty highway at 3 AM, single headlight fading into the distance

beats.say: What if you paid $300 a month instead? You’d be done in 12 months, paying only $381 in interest.
beats.visual: low angle shot of a cash envelope on wet asphalt, neon sign reflecting

beats.say: So why do we keep our heads in the sand?
beats.visual: silhouette of a person under an underpass, sodium light cutting across

beats.say: Psychologists call it the ostrich effect. We avoid bad news to reduce stress today.
beats.visual: extreme close of a credit card half-buried in sand, golden hour light

beats.say: But stress now or stress for 15 years? The math is clear.
beats.visual: high angle of a calendar with a single red circle on a rainy day, cold fluorescent

beats.say: Here’s the move: two minutes, same day each week. Open the app, look, then act.
beats.visual: back of a phone held over a ridge line at blue hour, hands steady

beats.say: No drama, no panic. Just the numbers.
beats.visual: empty office chair spinning under a single practical light, late night

beats.say: Because the $3,000 you ignore today becomes the $7,887 problem tomorrow.
beats.visual: extreme wide of a credit card on a desert road, sun setting behind

beats.say: Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: silhouette of a person walking into mist, city skyline in the distance, sodium light

caption: Ignoring your balance doesn’t make it go away. It just makes it more expensive. #MoneyPsychology #QuietMoney #DebtFree #PersonalFinance #OstrichEffect
description: The ostrich effect makes us avoid bad financial news, but ignoring a $3,000 credit card at 24% can cost you 15 years and $7,887. The fix? Two minutes a week to face the numbers.
first_comment: What’s the longest you’ve avoided checking a balance?

facts.claim: A $3,000 credit card at 24% APR with minimum payments (1% + interest, min $25) takes 183 months (~15 years) and $4,887 in interest.
facts.basis: Provided in the money fact sheet.

facts.claim: The same $3,000 at 24% APR paid with $300/month takes 12 months and $381 in interest.
facts.basis: Provided in the money fact sheet.

facts.claim: The ostrich effect is a documented psychological bias where people avoid information that may cause discomfort.

loop_map.big_question: Why does ignoring it make it worse?
loop_map.assume: If I don’t look, the problem stays small
loop_map.reveal: Interest never sleeps; the balance grows regardless
